questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The _____ that carry freight are called cars (in the United States) or wagons (in the United Kingdom).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “carry”. It names more than one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Train article, under the heading “Freight”.

questions.proof: There are hopper cars for sand, coal, ore and other granulous (sand-like) materials, flatbed cars for vehicles and machinery, tank cars for liquids, container cars for containers and even bottle cars for molten iron.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “A new word for _____ that also use tracks used by other trains outside the city is '''tram-trains'''.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “word”. It names more than one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Trains in the city” part of the Train article.

questions.proof: Trains which go along city roads are called Trams.
